parents.course: Advanced Topics in Food Science and Human Nutrition

ns2:section.sectionText: Biopsychology of Ingestive Behavior: Why do we eat what we eat? This course provides a taste of the science including both biological and psychological basis of ingestive behavior and the adoption of both healthy and maladaptive behaviors concerning eating and drinking. We will review and integrate historical theories with recent research on how we perceive flavor, the development of food preferences, and the biological basis of hunger, thirst, and satiety. Students will also have the opportunity to strengthen their critical thinking skills by participating on two debates in which equal number of arguments will be formulated to support or refute important issues in the field of food science and human nutrition.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Restricted to students with Senior or Graduate class standing. Restricted to Graduate - Urbana-Champaign or Undergrad - Urbana-Champaign.
